body.statement:
Assume \(L_r>0\), and define
\[
 d_{\max}=\begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
For every \(d\) with \(0<d<d_{\max}\), set
\[
 x(d)=\begin{cases}
 \sqrt{d/L_r},&d\le M^2/L_r,\\
 \{d+M^2/L_r\}/(2M),&d>M^2/L_r,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad a(d)=1-x(d).
\]
If a sequence of possibly randomized complete-log confidence sets is asymptotically \((1-\alpha)\)-honest uniformly over all experiments satisfying the declared structured assumptions, then, under each sign of the capped clipped-ramp member with start \(a(d)\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]
The elbow \(d=M^2/L_r\) is interior to \((0,d_{\max})\) exactly when \(L_r>M\). Among two-sign late-void witnesses whose residual profiles vanish on \([0,a]\), are bounded in absolute value by \(M\), and have Lipschitz modulus at most \(L_r\), the clipped profile is pointwise optimal, and the displayed bound is the optimized late-void envelope. For each selected two-sign clipped-ramp subexperiment the bound is attained asymptotically by the exact randomized allocation, but no global minimax attainment over the full structured class is claimed.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(g_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\).  First consider any admissible two-sign late-void residual pair \(\widetilde r^+=g\), \(\widetilde r^-=-g\), where \(g=0\) on \([0,a]\), \(|g(u)|\le M\), and \(g\) is \(L_r\)-Lipschitz.  For \(u>a\), the Lipschitz condition and \(g(a)=0\) give
\[
 |g(u)|=|g(u)-g(a)|\le L_r(u-a).
\]
Combining this inequality with the outcome bound yields
\[
 |g(u)|\le g_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}.
\]
The capped clipped ramp attains equality pointwise.  Hence every such witness has limiting two-sign causal separation at most
\[
 2\int_0^1 |g(u)|\,du
 \le 2\int_0^{1-a}\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds
 =:d(1-a),
\]
and the clipped ramp attains the last expression.  Direct integration gives
\[
 d(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L_rx^2,&L_rx\le M,\\
 2Mx-M^2/L_r,&L_rx>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
Thus \(d\) is continuous and strictly increasing on \([0,1]\), and
\[
 d(1)=
 \begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M,
 \end{cases}
 =d_{\max}.
\]
If \(L_r\le M\), then \(d_{\max}=L_r\le M^2/L_r\), so every \(d<d_{\max}\) is on the quadratic branch.  If \(L_r>M\), the clipping point \(x=M/L_r\) belongs to \((0,1)\) and has image \(M^2/L_r\).  Solving \(d=d(x)\) on the two branches gives exactly the displayed \(x(d)\).  Consequently
\[
 0<x(d)<1,\qquad a(d)=1-x(d)\in(0,1),
 \qquad d(x(d))=d.
\]
This also proves that the residual elbow is interior exactly when \(L_r>M\).

Fix \(d\in(0,d_{\max})\) and choose the capped clipped-ramp pair with start \(a_\star=a(d)\).  The capped-ramp membership proposition places both signs in the declared structured class.  With
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\},
\]
uniform asymptotic honesty therefore implies
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le\alpha.
\]
The sharp two-sign clipped-ramp theorem supplies
\[
 \Delta_n\ge d(1-a(d))=d,
 \qquad \eta_n\longrightarrow a(d)^c,
\]
and, under either sign,
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
Because \(\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}\subseteq
\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}\), continuity and monotonicity of \(z\mapsto[z]_+\) give
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[a(d)^c-2\alpha]_+
 =[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]

For completeness, the attaining allocation can be read directly from the common void component.  Outside the void event, the first nonzero treated outcome identifies the sign, so report the corresponding true singleton.  On the void, if \(\eta_n>2\alpha\), give unconditional void masses \(\alpha\), \(\alpha\), and \(\eta_n-2\alpha\) to the positive singleton, the negative singleton, and the two-target set.  If \(\alpha<\eta_n\le2\alpha\), give unconditional void masses \(\eta_n-\alpha\), \(\eta_n-\alpha\), and \(2\alpha-\eta_n\) to the two singletons and the empty set.  If \(\eta_n\le\alpha\), report the empty set on the void.  Each sign then has miscoverage at most \(\alpha\), and the only output of positive diameter is the two-target set, whose diameter is \(\Delta_n\ge d\).  Hence
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 = [\eta_n-2\alpha]_+
 \longrightarrow[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]
This is attainment only inside the selected pair.

Finally, suppose another admissible late-void residual pair starts at \(a'=1-x'\) and has limiting separation at least \(d\).  The pointwise envelope already proved implies \(d\le d(x')\).  Strict monotonicity of \(d\) gives \(x'\ge x(d)\), whence
\[
 (a')^c=(1-x')^c\le(1-x(d))^c.
\]
This certifies optimality within the stated constant-intensity late-void witness geometry.

For the exact diagnostic, set \(c=a_\star=1/2\), \(L_r=1/2\), \(M\ge1/4\), and \(\alpha=0.05\).  Then the clipped residual is the original linear ramp and
\[
 d(1/2)=\frac18,
 \qquad
 [(1/2)^{1/2}-0.1]_+
 =0.6071067811865475\ldots.
\]
With \(m_n=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), exact enumeration at the four smallest horizons gives
\[
 (\Delta_1,\Delta_2,\Delta_3,\Delta_4)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac14,\frac29,\frac3{16}\right)
\]
and
\[
 (\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3,\eta_4)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac34,\frac58,\frac{35}{48}\right).
\]
Every enumerated separation exceeds \(1/8\), and each void mass is exactly the product used in the common-subprobability proof.
Thus the result preserves the exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) obstruction.  It does not alter the separate positive calibration theorem, the directed \(13/32\) certificate, or the high-hazard \(0.442M\) result.
body.justification: This remains the constant-intensity all-confidence-set late-void converse optimized over the existing outcome bound and residual Lipschitz modulus.
body.gap: The linear residual ramp leaves separation unused after reaching the outcome bound; clipping exposes the residual elbow, while intensity optimization is handled by a separate pair-honesty theorem.
body.consumer: For any requested diameter below the maximal clipped separation, trial designers can read off the constant-intensity obstruction available under structured-class uniform honesty.
